doors.label: Tax cap
doors.sentence: "This city needs to spend within its means. No more frivolous expenses like the Centennial Square Revitalization Project. No need to raise property taxes or fees then." No formula, no cap, no glide path.

doors.label: Downtown order
doors.sentence: "STOP THE SWEEPS! Specifically, I would replace bylaw officers with outreach workers to help the homeless get back on their feet." No Public Order Team and no bylaw-hours position. The sentence is opposition to current enforcement, not a unified-command plan.

doors.label: Written program
doors.sentence: An authorized campaign site with a long-form platform covering homelessness, drug policy, law and order, Indigenous relations and the environment, plus dated posts through August 2026 and a candidate-submitted VoteMate profile. Written and current. No costed budget, no tax formula, no unit target, no implementation calendar.

cells.quote: We need outreach workers answering mental health calls, not police officers. More Crisis Response Community Led team, Integrated Mobile Crisis Response Team, and Victoria Integrated Community Outreach Team.
cells.why: M26b is civilian crisis response dispatched so the wrong responder stops absorbing officer time. CRCL is named. Same instrument. No dispatch criteria, no funding figure, no published diversion number.

cells.quote: Lift the prohibition on overnight sheltering in city parks! Better parks than sidewalks and doorways.
cells.why: M33 is consistent daytime sheltering bylaws. Lifting the parks prohibition is explicit disagreement. Context, same VoteMate block: the Parks Regulation Bylaw challenge is described at length on the campaign site.

cells.what: drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure)
cells.quote: I propose that we implement decriminalization of simple possession at the municipal level, by directing the police not to enforce s. 4 of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act.
cells.why: M33b's City-side instrument includes VicPD/CDSA enforcement around child-focused spaces. Directing police not to enforce s. 4 is explicit disagreement. Context: he would extend the same directive to licensed compassion clubs under s. 5.

M34–M37 reclaim named spaces and govern encampment removal. Blanket opposition to sweeps is explicit disagreement. Context, separate VoteMate bullet not scored elsewhere: "No more fences on Pandora Avenue!"

cells.what: tax glide path (capped on the residential rate)
cells.quote: This city needs to spend within its means. No more frivolous expenses like the Centennial Square Revitalization Project. No need to raise property taxes or fees then.
cells.why: Commits against raising the residential rate, with no cap, no formula, no year-path, no override rule. The instrument named is cutting a capital project, not a tax rule. Context, same profile: "No property tax raises; let's live within our means instead." is the same claim and is not scored again.

cells.what: CRD cost and the Goldstream plant
business, downtown, one mandate not a new office
capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees
Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5.
cells.quote: The City of Victoria has yet to take an official stance against this assault on the hard-won Indigenous rights. It could bring forth the matter to the Union of BC Municipalities for debate, or seek to intervene against the government in the aforementioned appeal.
cells.why: Commits to a City advocacy action on DRIPA. No standing government-to-government table, no procurement target, no place-name programme, no cultural-protocol package, no urban Indigenous liaison. Context, VoteMate, not scored separately: "I fully endorse Indigenous housing initiatives like the Rematriate Stewardship Project."

cells.what: tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated)
cells.quote: Let's bring back the Renters' Advisory Committee! Every tenant deserves a voice at City Hall.
cells.why: Commits to a tenant-voice body. No demoviction bylaw, no STR licensing, no indoor-heat standard. Context from the 21 Jul essay, not scored separately: wrongful eviction is named as a cause of return to homelessness, with no instrument attached.

cells.quote: Let's spend less on law enforcement, and more on housing.
cells.why: Commits to housing as the homelessness instrument, which is the Housing First half of M11. No 50% unsheltered target, no STEP throughput, no quarterly count. Context, 21 Jul essay: he names Housing First, then prefers a more gradual client-centric path than "rushing them into shoeboxes" — that is a comparable instrument, not opposition to housing-led response. Context, VoteMate, not scored separately: "Let's prioritize drug users in recovery for supportive housing and services."

cells.what: childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is $0 → M13d)
mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38)
cells.quote: This city needs less private vehicles and more public transit. Then let's turn excess parking space into more useful amenities.
cells.why: Commits to mode shift and to converting parking. No adaptive-signal programme, no Vision Zero audit, no named corridor, no calming design. Transit service itself is not a City decision (M23b); parking conversion is a City lever, but it is not the cluster's instrument set. Context, campaign site, not scored separately: planning for Uber, Evo and Waymo and fewer private cars.

cells.what: walking and transit the City controls

cells.quote: Pandora Avenue needs its own public washroom. No more excuses!
cells.why: M24b is public bathrooms as walking infrastructure. Same instrument, named, with a location. No accessibility audit, no hours standard, no city-wide count.

cells.what: VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force)
cells.quote: Let's defund VicPD and allocate the difference to address poverty crime at the source.
cells.why: M29 is a funding-formula settlement and a convene-and-publish regional review, not a defund. Explicit disagreement with VicPD funding as currently constituted. Police-Board appointment and a civil-rights defender, from the campaign site, are a different sentence and are used as context on row 51, not as a second mark here.

cells.what: safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target

cells.quote: More pedestrian priority zones and bike lanes!
cells.why: M45b is pedestrianisation. Pedestrian priority zones are the same instrument, named. No signature-project shortlist, no referendum, nothing on M45c. Bike lanes in the same bullet are not given a second mark.

cells.what: culture, sport, and the arts funding floor
local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging

cells.quote: While we're at it, the municipality should also divest its holdings in oil and gas corporations.
cells.why: Commits to a municipal climate instrument (portfolio divestment). Comparable to M58's delivery of the Climate Leadership Plan, not the same as the 50% / 2030 target set, district energy, or seismic. Context, same block, not scored separately: staff study of eliminating gasoline dependence, and rooftop solar on the remaining 80% after a greenery ordinance.

cells.what: trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness
cells.quote: Tokyo, among the most densely populated cities in the world, has decreed in 2001 that every new building with a sizeable rooftop must dedicate at least twenty percent of its surface to greenery. We could at least contemplate such an ordinance for this city.
cells.why: Agrees with a greenery ordinance as a goal and names the instrument, without committing to adopt it. Comparable to the trees/ecosystems half of M59–M63. No 5,000-tree target, no 35% canopy, no emergency-preparedness position. Mode share is inside the sentence already scored on row 27.

cells.quote: I would amend the code of conduct for council members to allow any resident to file a complaint, as many have been clamouring for.
cells.why: Commits to a resident-complaint integrity instrument. Comparable to M79b's Integrity Commissioner / MNP conflict machinery, not the same office and not a 60-day consultation-response standard. Context: seeking appointment to the Police Board and "press for the appointment of a civil rights defender among the public"; VoteMate "More transparency and less closed meetings."

cells.quote: We need more transparency! Let's release investigation reports into bylaw officer misconduct.
cells.why: Commits to FOI-side disclosure of a named class of records. No lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee position, no remuneration rule. The judicial-review petition is a citizen action, not a City-office record, and is cited only as context that the 2026 sentence is live.

cells.what: neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans
community surveys, turnout and ballot access
Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic)
